title: Viability of Bioprinted Cellular Constructs Using a Three Dispenser Cartesian Printer
protocol: Combine calcium chloride dehydrate (1.5 wt%), sodium chloride (0.9 wt%), and porcine gelatin (2 wt%) in distilled water.
Boil the mixture for 2 minutes to create a 100 mM gelatin solution.
Pour 5 ml of the gelatin/calcium solution into 100 mm standard petri dishes.
Swirl the solution around to make an even coating on the surface.
Place the petri dishes on a flat surface in the fridge to gel overnight (at least 8 hours before use).
Add titanium dioxide (0.3 wt%) to the gelatin/CaCl2 solution for increased opacity.
Stir the mixture for 10 minutes.
Autoclave the gelatin/TiO2 solution on the liquids cycle for 30 minutes to sterilize it.
Add 3 ml of the gelatin/TiO2 solution to the surface of the previously prepared gelatin plates.
Swirl the mixture to ensure even distribution across the surface.
Allow to gel in the refrigerator overnight (at least 8 hours before use).
Use the substrates within 3 days.
Dissolve 1 g of sodium alginate in 100 ml of distilled water.
Add an aqueous solution of sodium periodate (0.25 M, 0.25 mmol) to produce a 5% oxidation solution.
Stir the solution for 19 hours at room temperature.
Add 40 ml ethylene glycol to the solution after 24 hours to terminate the reaction.
Dissolve 2.5 g of sodium chloride in the solution.
Add an excess amount of ethyl alcohol (2:1 ratio) to precipitate the oxidized alginates.
Centrifuge the solution at 1,000 x g to collect the precipitates and re-dissolve them in distilled water.
Repeat the ethanol wash.
Freeze-dry the oxidized alginate pellets and store at -20°C until ready for use.
Determine the degree of oxidation by measuring the percentage of sodium periodate consumed before being terminated by ethylene glycol.
Prepare a potassium iodide solution (20% w/v, pH 7.0 sodium phosphate buffer).
Prepare a thyodene solution (10% w/v, pH 7.0 sodium phosphate buffer).
Mix the oxidized alginate with the potassium iodide and thyodene solutions at room temperature.
Gradually drop the reacted alginate and sodium periodate solution into the mixture of potassium iodide and thyodene solutions.
Measure the absorbance of the mixture spectrophotometrically at 426 nm.
Dissolve 1 g of 5% oxidized alginate in a 0.1 M MES buffer, pH = 4.
Add 0.54 mmol EDC and 0.27 mmol NHS at a 2:1 ratio to form amide intermediate.
Add 0.28 mmol peptide for coupling to the backbone of the alginate polymer via terminal amine.
Stir solution at room temperature overnight.
Stop the coupling reaction by adding 2.5 g sodium chloride to the solution.
Add an excess amount of ethyl alcohol (2:1 ratio) to precipitate oxidized alginates.
Centrifuge the mixture at 4,000 x g for 5 min to collect precipitates.
Aspirate media in the cell culture hood and re-dissolve precipitates in distilled water.
Repeat ethanol wash.
Freeze-dry the precipitates until they become completely dried (appearing as a white powdery substance).
Store the freeze-dried precipitates in the -20°C fridge for later use.
Culture human adipose tissue stromal cells (hADSC’s) in 75 cm treated cell culture flasks (T75 flasks).
Cover T75 flasks with 15 ml low glucose DMEM containing 10% fetal bovine serum, 1% penicillin-streptomycin, 1% glutamine, and 1% antimycin.
Change the media in the cell culture hood every two days until cells reach confluency (80-90%).
Once confluent, transfer T75 flasks to the cell culture hood.
Aspirate all of the cell culture media off of the hADSC’s.
Rinse with 5 ml of Dulbecco’s Phosphate-Buffered Saline with calcium and magnesium (DPBS ++).
Aspirate the DPBS++ off of the cells.
While in the hood, make a solution by mixing 1 ml trypsin and 4 ml DPBS++ for each flask.
Add 5 ml of the trypsin/DPBS++ to each T75 flask and place them in the incubator for 2 min.
Remove the flasks after 2 minutes.
Lightly tap the sides of the flasks to loosen the cells from the bottoms.
Look at each flask under a microscope to ensure the cells are suspended.
Place the flasks back in the cell culture hood.
Add 3 ml of appropriate cell culture media to each flask to end the trypsin reaction.
Transfer the cell-laden media from each flask into a 50 ml conical tube.
Centrifuge them at 1,000 x g for 5 minutes.
Aspirate the supernatant and resuspend the cells in 2 ml of cell culture media.
Count the cells using a hemocytometer under the microscope.
Aliquot the amount of media containing approximately 1.3 million cells into a 15 ml conical tube.
Centrifuge the 15 ml conical tube for 5 minutes at 1,000 x g.
Resuspend the cell pellet in aqueous alginate solution to achieve a concentration of 1.3 million cells per milliliter.
Load the cell-laden solution into a sterile printer-compatible 3 ml syringe and attach a sterile 22 G plastic tip.
Turn on the bioprinter, each of the dispenser computers, and the recirculating water bath.
Set the recirculating water bath temperature manually for the gelation mechanism.
Manually set printing parameters for each dispenser.
Set the dispense volume to 230 nl.
Set the number of backsteps to 0.
Set the dispense rate to 10 μl/sec.
Open the design software and the program for viewing the USB camera’s display on the computer.
Manually enter coordinates for a 5 x 5 dot array with 2.4 mm spacing between drops in the software.
Set the distance between tip end and substrate surface to 0.1 mm.
Set the height syringe is lifted between depositions to 20 mm.
Set the amount of time per deposition to 1 sec.
Save the program and send it to the robot.
Place the gelatin/TiO2-containing Petri dish on the 4 °C printer stage.
Close and lock the chamber door.
Use the PLC to initialize ultraviolet light sources.
Sterilize the chamber for 90 sec.
Once sterilization is complete, open the chamber.
Load the syringe containing hADSC’s suspended in alginate into Gun 1.
Close and lock the chamber door.
Use the PLC to turn on the fan system.
Wait 30 sec for equilibrium internal pressure.
Run the program containing the geometrical pathway and printing parameters on the computer.
Watch the USB camera’s display on the computer during the printing process to confirm accurate and uniform printing.
Once printing has finished, allow the constructs to gel for 40 min.
Cover constructs not to be imaged immediately in DMEM.
Store covered constructs in the incubator until imaging time.
Prepare a staining solution containing calcein AM and ethidium homodimer-1 according to kit instructions.
Add 20 μl of ethidium homodimer-1 and 5 μl of calcein AM to 10 ml DPBS++.
Immerse bioprinted constructs in the staining solution for 15 min in the dark.
Image stained constructs using a confocal microscope system at days 0 and 8.
Take multiple pictures of each construct with Z-stack parameters set to 30 optical slices over 300 μm depth.
Count cells manually; yellow or green cells are alive, red cells are dead.
Calculate cell viability as (number of live cells) / (total number of cells) * 100%.
Calculate cell proliferation as (live cell count on day 8) / (live cell count on day 0) * 100%.
Make the phalloidins working solution by diluting 5 μl of the methanolic stock solution with 200 μl of DPBS++.
Store the phalloidin working solution at -20°C until use.
Prepare a 300 μM stock solution of DAPI stain.
Make the DAPI working solution by diluting the stock solution 1:100 in DPBS++ to obtain a 3 μM solution.
Store the DAPI working solution at -20°C until use.
Completely submerge the sample in 4% paraformaldehyde.
Incubate for 1 hour at room temperature.
Wash three times with DPBS++, allowing the solution to sit for 5 minutes each wash.
Transfer the gel sample from the well to a glass slide, flipping the gel over in the process.
Immerse the gel in 0.1% Triton X-100 in DPBS++ for 10 minutes.
Wash three times with DPBS++, allowing 5 minutes for each wash.
Stain the printed constructs with phalloidin by immersing them in the working solution.
Cover with foil and incubate for 4 hours.
Remove the phalloidin stain and wash three times with DPBS++.
The first wash should be fast, the latter washes should sit for 5 minutes each.
Stain the printed constructs with DAPI by immersing them in the DAPI working solution.
Cover with foil.
Incubate at room temperature for 30 min.
Wash three times with DPBS++.
Allow each wash to sit for 5 min.
Observe and image the samples on a confocal microscope system.
